standout internals. Three things beyond `docs/` are worth declaring:

   `handler-contract.md` both document `AppFailure` at `standout::cli::AppFailure`; it
   does not exist in the pinned standout 9.0.0. I found the working API by writing
   candidate `use` statements and reading rustc's errors — including its "there is a
   method `binary` with a similar name" suggestion for `TestResult` — rather than by
   opening the crate. Same technique located `standout::dispatch::Extensions` and
   established that `CommandContext::app_state` is `Rc`, not `Arc`. Details in the docs
   gaps answer.

   the wording of the unknown-`--json`-field diagnostic, and compact (rather than

   `--json` fields alphabetically; I deliberately did *not* copy that, since it is an

answers.docs.gaps:
**`AppFailure` is documented but absent from standout 9.0.0.** Quoted in full in the
friction answer. Two pages document it — `docs/topics/error-handling.md` ("An
application-owned status and diagnostic") and
`docs/crates/dispatch/topics/handler-contract.md` ("Owner-declared failures", which
says "Standout recognizes only these two concrete types" and exposes them as
"`RunErrorKind::App` and `RunErrorKind::External`"). `docs/topics/testing.md` repeats it
a third time: "For an `AppFailure` or an `ExternalFailure`, `stdout()` is empty …".
Only `ExternalFailure` actually exists. Since it is the only available seam that pins
both status and stderr bytes, an application-owned domain error currently has to be
declared as though it were relayed from an external operation — the exact distinction
the docs draw between the two types cannot be expressed.

**`CommandContext::app_state` is `Rc`, but the testing recipe uses `Arc`.**
`handler-contract.md` gives the struct as:

> ```rust
> pub struct CommandContext {
>     pub command_path: Vec<String>,
>     pub app_state: Rc<Extensions>,
>     pub extensions: Extensions,
> }
> ```

and then, ~200 lines later under "Testing with App State", contradicts itself:

> ```rust
>     use std::sync::Arc;
>     …
>     let ctx = CommandContext {
>         command_path: vec!["list".into()],
>         app_state: Arc::new(app_state),
>         extensions: Extensions::new(),
>     };
> ```

Copying that recipe gives:

```
150 |             app_state: std::sync::Arc::new(state),
    |                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ expected `Rc<Extensions>`, found `Arc<Extensions>`
```

The struct definition is the correct one. The same page also describes `app_state` in
prose as "Wrapped in `Arc` for cheap cloning", which is wrong in the same direction.

**`Extensions` is never imported in any example.** No page states its module path. It
is `standout::dispatch::Extensions`, not `standout::cli::Extensions`.

**`#[dispatch(nested)]` never shows the clap side.** `dispatch-attributes.md` gives:

> ```rust
> #[derive(Dispatch)]
> #[dispatch(handlers = handlers)]
> enum Commands {
>     #[dispatch(nested)]
>     Pr(PrCommands),
> }
> ```

That enum does not derive `Subcommand`, so the example never has to say how clap is
told that `PrCommands` is a nested subcommand enum rather than an `Args` struct. Every
other `Dispatch` example in the docs derives `Subcommand` alongside it, so the omission
reads as an oversight. The working spelling is `#[command(subcommand)]` on the same
variant. Without it the derive fails on the clap side, and the docs give no hint which
of `#[command(subcommand)]`, `#[command(flatten)]`, or an intermediate `Args` struct is
intended — the latter two produce a different command tree.

**Not a gap, but the single most useful undocumented-by-example detail** was in
`templating.md`: "The engine consumes exactly one final newline" plus "The process edge
appends exactly one newline", with the table of template-source-to-rendered-string. A
spec with byte-exact expected output is unbuildable without that paragraph, and it is
stated precisely. Worth keeping prominent.
answers.friction:
**`AppFailure` does not exist.** `docs/topics/error-handling.md` says:

> ```rust
> use standout::cli::{AppFailure, HandlerResult};
> ```
> `AppFailure` is the seam for a domain error whose exit status and stderr bytes
> the application's own specification pins.

and gives, as its worked example, almost exactly this application's error line:

> ```rust
> return Err(AppFailure::new(1, "ghlike: repository not found: demo/gamma\n")?.into());
> ```

Building that gave:

```
error[E0432]: unresolved import `standout::cli::AppFailure`
 --> src/handlers.rs:5:21
  |
5 | use standout::cli::{AppFailure, CommandContext, Output};
  |                     ^^^^^^^^^^ no `AppFailure` in `cli`
```

Not under `standout::AppFailure`, `standout::dispatch::AppFailure`,
`standout_dispatch::AppFailure`, `standout::cli::error::AppFailure`, or
`standout::error::AppFailure` either — and rustc offered no similar-name suggestion,
so nothing is merely renamed. `ExternalFailure`, documented on the same page, *is*
present in `standout::cli` and has the same constructor shape and the same
verbatim-stderr / declared-status contract, so that is what I used. This cost the most
time of anything in the task, because the exit-code and stderr-byte contract is the
part of SPEC.md with the least slack.

**`Extensions` has no documented path.** `handler-contract.md`'s test recipe writes
`let mut app_state = Extensions::new();` with no `use` line anywhere on the page.
`standout::cli::Extensions` does not resolve; `standout::dispatch::Extensions` does.

**The table layout rule versus `tabular()`.** `intro-to-tabular.md` says, of bounded
columns:

> Without `rows=` a bounded column has nothing to grow it: it lands on its `min`, and
> with no `"fill"` (or fractional) column in the table any leftover terminal width is
> added to the rightmost bounded column instead, regardless of its `max`.

I could not tell from that whether the leftover-width rule still applies when `rows=`
*is* passed. If it does, the last column gets padded and every row of `pr list` ends in
trailing spaces, which fails the spec's byte-exact output. Rather than gamble on it I
used `pad_right` with widths resolved in the view — see workarounds.

answers.summary:
`ghlike`, the forge client described in SPEC.md, complete and working. `cargo build`
succeeds with no warnings from the crate, `cargo test` passes 28 tests, and I verified
every spec case by running the built binary.

Layout (single crate, but split along the ownership line the docs teach):

- `src/forge.rs` — the frozen forge state. CLI-free: no clap, no standout, no
  rendering. Owns the model and the lookups.
- `src/views.rs` — CLI-owned view DTOs, plus the resolved column widths for the two
  tables.
- `src/handlers.rs` — `#[handler]` adapters, one per command, grouped in modules
  (`auth`, `repo`, `pr`, `pr::checks`) so the four `list`/`view` names do not collide.
- `src/machine.rs` — `--json <fields>`: field-list parsing, per-field JSON assembly,
  and the raw-byte emission.
- `src/main.rs` — the clap tree, `#[derive(Dispatch)]` wiring, `App` assembly, and the
  `standout-test` harness suite.
- `src/templates/{auth/status,repo/view,pr/list,pr/view,pr/checks/list}.jinja` and
  `src/styles/default.css`.

The command tree is three `#[dispatch(nested)]` groups (`auth`, `repo`, `pr`) with
`checks` nested a level deeper under `pr`, so registration paths are `auth.status`,
`repo.view`, `pr.list`, `pr.view`, `pr.checks.list` and templates resolve by the
path-to-slash convention.

Behavior confirmed against the spec:

- All five human outputs are byte-exact, with no trailing whitespace and exactly one
  final newline. `pr checks list 3` (a PR with no checks) writes zero bytes and
  exits 0.
- `--json` on `pr list`, `pr view`, and `pr checks list` emits pure JSON — compact,
  one trailing newline, objects carrying exactly the requested fields in the
  requested order, `number` a JSON number and `draft` a JSON boolean.
- Exit codes: 0 success; 1 for unknown repo, unknown PR, and unknown `--json` field
  (empty stdout, verbatim `ghlike: …` line on stderr); 2 for a group without a
  subcommand, an unknown subcommand, and an unknown flag (empty stdout, guidance
  on stderr).
- `--help` works and exits 0 at every level, including the two group levels.
- Human output is styled on a color-capable terminal; `--json` output is not, even
  under a forced `--output term`.

Two design decisions worth naming:

- `--json` returns `Output::Binary`, so the framework writes the document to stdout
  verbatim: no template, no theme, no pager, no prose. That is what makes the
  "byte-boring even on an attended terminal" clause hold structurally rather than by
  convention.
- The table layout rule (single-space separator, every column but the last padded to
  its widest rendered cell, header included) is done with `pad_right` in the template
  over widths resolved in the view — the same shape standout's own help template uses
  with `options_width` / `subcommands_width`. See the workarounds answer for why I did
  not use `tabular()`.
answers.workarounds:
**`ExternalFailure` standing in for `AppFailure`.** Every domain error — unknown repo,
unknown PR, unknown `--json` field — is declared with
`ExternalFailure::new(1, "ghlike: …\n")?`. These are application-owned verdicts, so
`AppFailure` is the semantically right type; it does not exist in 9.0.0. The observable
contract is identical (status 1, verbatim stderr bytes, no `Error:` prefix, empty
stdout), and the only difference is that a capture caller sees
`RunErrorKind::External` instead of `RunErrorKind::App`. If `AppFailure` appears in a
later release, the fix is a type rename at three call sites in `src/handlers.rs` and
`src/machine.rs`.

**Column widths live in the view data.** `PrListView` carries a `widths` field and
`CheckListView` likewise, and the templates align with
`{{ value | pad_right(widths.number) }}`. This mirrors how standout's own help template
aligns its sections against `HelpData`'s `options_width` / `subcommands_width`, and it
is the only approach I could guarantee produces no trailing whitespace on the last
column. The cost is a real one and I am flagging it rather than hiding it: `widths`
is presentation data sitting in the serializable view, so it shows up in
`ghlike pr list --output json` alongside `pull_requests`. It does *not* leak into
`--json`, which is the machine contract SPEC.md actually defines, and which builds its
document field by field. If `tabular(..., rows=...)` is in fact guaranteed not to pad
the trailing column, that would be the better implementation and would delete both
`widths` structs.

**`<number>` is parsed as `String`, not `u32`.** SPEC.md assigns "unknown number" to
exit 1 with `ghlike: no pull request found: <number>`. Taking the positional as `u32`
would route `ghlike pr view abc` to a clap type error (exit 2) instead, splitting one
specified behavior across two exit codes on a distinction the spec does not draw. So
the handler takes text and does its own lookup: anything the forge does not know —
`9`, `abc`, `-1` — is the one domain error, and the rejected text is echoed back
verbatim. `ghlike pr checks list <unknown>` reports the same error, which SPEC.md does
not specify either way.

**A reachable `unreachable!` in `src/machine.rs`.** `pull_request()` and `check()`
match on field names that `select()` has already validated against the same constant
list, and the `_` arm panics. The two functions are private to the module and the
validation is three lines above the call site, so the invariant is local — but it is an
invariant held by convention rather than by the type system, which a field-name enum
would fix.

**Duplicate `--json` fields are silently de-duplicated** and surrounding whitespace is
trimmed, so `--json " number , number "` is `--json number`. SPEC.md says nothing about
either; I picked the forgiving reading. An empty field name (`--json ""`, or the empty
element in `--json a,,b`) is rejected as an unknown field, which produces the slightly
odd `ghlike: unknown JSON field: ` with nothing after the colon.
